title: Designing AI Learning Experiences for K-12: Emerging Works, Future Opportunities and a Design Framework
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '20)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the emerging need for K-12 artificial intelligence (AI) literacy resources and asks how existing AI education work can be organized into practical guidance for educators and researchers. Rather than testing a new intervention with participants, the authors conduct an exploratory review of K-12 AI and AI-literacy-related literature and tools to identify common patterns, gaps, and promising design directions.

The paper synthesizes 49 works spanning elementary, middle school, high school, and unspecified K-12 contexts. It organizes these works using AI literacy competencies and design considerations adapted from Long and Magerko’s framework, then extends that framework with nine future opportunities and eleven additional design guidelines tailored to K-12 learning. The review includes a range of tools, curricula, workshops, and classroom activities, many of which involve block-based programming, tangible/robotic systems, visualizations, and guided activities for students and teachers.

Its main conclusion is that current K-12 AI learning experiences tend to emphasize accessibility, engagement, and hands-on programming, but often under-address ethics, gradual scaffolding, identity/backgrounds, parental support, and explicit explanations of AI capabilities and limitations. The paper argues that future AI education efforts should more deliberately support diverse learners, involve teachers and parents more fully, and integrate AI learning into broader K-12 subjects. It is a conceptual and survey-based contribution intended to guide future design rather than report outcome effects from a single study.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic AI literacy / AI learning experience category rather than a specific commercial or research product.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a conceptual review and design framework for K-12 AI literacy experiences. It surveys many AI education tools and curricula, but does not evaluate a single named generative AI product or chatbot.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual and exploratory review/design framework paper, not an empirical study evaluating an AI tool with participants. It synthesizes prior work and proposes guidelines rather than reporting outcome data.
impact_tier_rationale: No quantitative impact estimates or subgroup outcome data are reported in this paper. The paper does not test interventions or measure effects, so there is no evaluable impact on literacy outcomes.
